newsitem.title: USA: Whitman cites difficult industry conditions.
newsitem.headline: Whitman cites difficult industry conditions.

text.p: Whitman Corp, which reported lower 1997 second quarter profits, said Thursday that some difficult industry conditions affected each of its businesses in the period.

"For Pepsi General, the principal issue was pricing," said Whitman chairman Bruce Chelberg in a news release. "For Midas, it was weak retail demand, which continued to affect the entire automotive service industry. And Hussmann's record domestic performance was offset by weak results in the U.K."
Chelberg said the company is taking steps to address these issues at each operating company.

Earlier today, Whitman reported 1997 second quarter earnings fell to $33.7 million or $0.33 a share from $41.7 million or $0.39 in the same period a year ago. Sales of $803.6 million for the second quarter of 1997 rose more than four percent from the second quarter of 1996.

In the second quarter, Whitman announced a plan to spin-off Hussmann and Midas to shareholders. Completion of the plan requires a tax-free ruling by the Internal Revenue Service for the company and its shareholders.
Whitman repeated that it will likely take some special charges later this year for the transactions, although it has yet to determine the nature, size, or timing of the charges.

Pepsi-Cola General Bottlers had sales of $392.5 million for the second quarter, up from $384.5 million last year. Operating profit in the quarter fell due to losses from the company's expanded international operations and a charge for a reduction in staff.

Midas International's sales and revenues totaled $160.3 million for the quarter, compared with sales of $161.7 million in the second quarter a year ago. Operating profit for the quarter declined by $5.2 million to $22 million.
Midas' results reflect an industry-wide slow-down in retail demand in the United States and a less favorable product mix in its domestic market.

Hussmann's sales rose to $250.8 million for the second quarter from $226 million last year. Operating profit totaled $21.3 million for the second quarter, compared with $21.8 million for the second quarter a year ago.
Hussmann's results reflect the impact of lower sales and margins in the United Kingdom and a less favorable product mix in Mexico.
Shares of Whitman were trading off 3/8 to 26-1/4.
